scale: human_score is a 1-5 rubric (5 = fully policy-compliant + correct; 1 = wrong / hallucinated / non-compliant)
provenance: AUTHOR-CURATED gold labels (single annotator), NOT independent human annotation. A directional calibration probe for judge-vs-human drift, not a validated inter-annotator gold standard. v2 (2026-08-22): CORRECTED. v1's reference responses cited policy that the system does not implement — a $200 entertainment limit (real: $150), city-specific lodging caps for New York/Austin (real: flat $400), a '$500 domestic flight approval' tier (real: flat $200 transport), a 'gifts' category (does not exist), per-person meal scaling (real: flat $75), and travel-class rules (none exist). Two cases also contradicted the coordinator's specification by treating refusal-to-submit as correct, when an over-limit expense must still be submitted and flagged for review. Calibrating the judge against v1 would have rewarded hallucinated policy. Ground truth is src/mcp_servers/expense/mock_db.py:POLICY_LIMITS. See docs/notes/evaluation-robustness-roadmap.md P1.6.
